parts: Take that passing test and turn it over.
把那张通过的试卷翻过来。
There is an old copy tucked behind it.
后面夹着一份旧卷。
Same question. Same answer, right down to the last symbol.
同一道题，答案连最后一个符号都相同。
Suppose Blue saw that copy in training.
假如蓝模型训练时见过它，
Our green check still tells us what it answered.
绿勾仍能说明它答对了。
The interesting question is what happens
真正的问题是：
when we pull the copy away.
拿走旧卷，它还会做吗？
delivery: Begin quietly as if you turned over a real test paper, lift gently on the last question.

parts: Go back to the shipping rule.
回到那个免邮规则。
At a hundred dollars, memorizing zero buys you the point.
一百美元那题，背个零也能得分。
Now slide the threshold to one twenty.
现在把门槛挪到一百二十美元。
Try an order for one nineteen.
拿一百一十九美元的订单试试。
The old shortcut still says free.
照搬旧答案，还是免邮。
The new rule says eight dollars.
按新规则，运费是八美元。
When test material gets into training, we call that contamination.
测试材料混进训练集，就叫数据污染。
A fresh case gives those two explanations a chance to disagree.
换道新题，两种解释才有机会分开。
With the training data in hand, we can go looking for a copy.
有训练数据，就能回头找副本。
Put a little window over three neighboring tokens.
拿个小窗口罩住三个相邻词元。
Slide it along the test item.
沿着试题滑动，
Look for those exact runs in the corpus.
在语料中找完全一样的片段。
The lecture's thirteen-token window works the same way.
讲义中的十三词元窗口也是这个道理。
A shared heading can light up by accident.
两篇文章共用页眉，也会亮灯。
A paraphrase can slip right through.
试题一旦改写，又可能完全对不上。
The match tells you where to look; you decide what to remove.
匹配给出线索，再决定删片段还是删整篇。
What if all we can see is the model's output probabilities?
如果只能看到模型给出的概率呢？
Take three independent test questions.
取三道相互独立的测试题。
Keep each answer stuck to its own question.
每道题和自己的答案贴在一起。
Now shuffle the cards, not the answers.
打乱卡片顺序，题和答案仍成对。
Give the model the whole stack as a sequence of text.
把整叠卡当成一段文本。
We can score how much probability it puts on that sequence.
再看模型给这个顺序分了多少概率。
Do the same for the published order.
原来公开的顺序，也算一次。
Add more cards and score a bunch of shuffles.
再加几张卡，多打乱几次。
Most land in this little cluster.
大部分重排落在这一小团。
The published order is the gold dot. Why is it way out there?
金点是公开顺序，为什么它孤零零在右边？
A model that remembers the stack has a reason to like it.
背过整叠的模型，当然更认这个顺序。
But these questions have to be exchangeable under the fresh-data assumption.
这里有个条件：没见过时，题目次序应当可交换。
Put dates on the cards, and chronological order gets an advantage for free.
给卡片加日期，按时间排序就天然更顺。
Now the shuffle is answering a different question.
这时打乱顺序，测的就成了另一件事。
You can save yourself some detective work by designing for freshness up front.
在出卷时就考虑新鲜度，能少做不少排查。
Freeze the model version and mark its training cutoff.
固定模型版本，标出训练截止点。
Put the test on the far side of that line.
到线的另一侧找题。
LiveCodeBench dates its programming problems, so you can pick a later window.
LiveCodeBench 按发布日期挑选较新的编程题。
Keep another set out of public circulation for a final check.
另留一套未公开的题做最后验收。
On the next run, write down which model and which test you actually used.
下次跑分，记清模型和题库的版本。
A fresh exam can still be the wrong exam.
题是新的，也可能考错了东西。
My shop needs a shipping spreadsheet someone can use tomorrow.
网店要的是店员明天能用的运费表。
There are coupons, partial refunds, and files other people have to open.
里面有优惠券、部分退款，还有要交付的文件。
That distance between the test and the real job is what ecological validity is about.
生态效度问的是：这场考试离真实工作有多远？
GDPval starts from professional deliverables.
GDPval 从实际职业交付件出题。
MedHELM separates jobs like drafting a clinical note and supporting a decision.
MedHELM 把整理临床记录和支持决策分开测。
A score goes further when its task looks like yours.
考的活儿越像你的，分数就越有用。
So give both systems the same tools, time limit, and unseen orders.
给两套系统相同的工具、时限和新订单。
Set aside the orders right on the boundary.
把踩着门槛的订单单独列出来。
Then add a nasty one: refund half of a one-twenty order.
再出道难的：一百二十美元的订单退一半。
Write the rule before either model gets to work.
模型开始做之前，先把规则定好。
Recompute shipping on the amount left.
按退款后的金额重算运费。
Maybe Blue is quicker. Purple gets the boundary right.
蓝模型可能更快，紫模型却把边界做对了。
Both miss the refund case.
退款这题，两个都错。
Now you know what to fix and what to keep with a person.
现在知道该修哪类题，哪类先交给人。
Bring back the first six tiles.
把开头那六个词元拿回来。
Blue really is better at predicting the lead-in.
蓝模型的确更擅长预测前面几格。
For arithmetic, the tile you hired it to fill is the last one.
可要它答算术题，你要的是最后一格。
A score can be exactly right about the tile it measures.
分数可以把它量的那格说得很准。
Before you let it pick a model for you, look beside it.
拿它选模型之前，再往旁边看看。
Which tile never made it onto the test?
哪一格压根没进考卷？
delivery: Quiet concentration, with a clear beat before the final question and a warm ending.
